findings.claim: The shared-name cleanup runs in every store job, so the first new-style store run on any branch deletes hail-store.tar.gz, which the B2 to B5 branches still read and write. The records say only main's job removes it.
findings.evidence: PyYAML parse: the publish step has keys ['env', 'name', 'run'] and no 'if', so the cleanup runs for every ref. Live release (read only, gh api repos/carson14dy/RoofingApp/releases/tags/hail-store): one asset, hail-store.tar.gz, 72,068,928 bytes, updated 2026-10-20T02:22:42Z. Readers on the other branches: git show claude/hail-b3:website/hail.py line 94 sets STORE_URL to .../hail-store.tar.gz, and that branch's store job publishes it (its line 302). git show claude/hail-b5:.github/workflows/hail-store.yml lines 365-366 download it for carried station ids in a continue-on-error step. The records disagree with the code: docs/DECISIONS.md lines 744-745 say main's job removes that asset, and tests/test_hail.py line 1678 says only main's job removes the earlier shared-name asset. The push of this revision to claude/hail-b1 triggers this job (the workflow file is in its own paths filter), so the deletion happens on that push. Fix: give the cleanup step if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main', or keep it everywhere and record the readers and the effect in D34. Decide before pushing.

findings.claim: The header promise 'A failed run leaves the last published asset in place' is false for an upload that fails after the old asset has been deleted.
findings.evidence: gh 2.89.0 'gh release upload --help', line 6: 'When using --clobber, existing assets are deleted before new assets are uploaded.' The upload step (line 87) uses --clobber. So an upload that fails after the delete leaves no hail-store-main.tar.gz. main's builds then read a 404 and show 'Hail history is unavailable: the history download failed: hail-store-main.tar.gz: not published (HTTP 404). This is not the same as no hail.' (the same text reproduced for the 404 path), until the next successful store job, which runs daily at 12:43 UTC. A build that reads during the delete-to-upload window gets the same 404. This is the mechanism from the help text, not reproduced against the live release, which needs a write. The same promise appears in website.yml lines 106-107 ('a failed or missing store job leaves the last published asset in place'). Fix: correct both comments and D34, or keep a second asset as a fallback.

findings.claim: A failed lookup of the shared asset is treated as 'nothing to remove', so the cleanup skips the removal and the job still passes.
findings.evidence: A step with no shell key runs as bash -e {0} (GitHub Actions docs: the unspecified shell on Linux is bash -e {0}; pipefail comes only with an explicit bash). Reproduction: the publish step's run text, extracted from the YAML, run under bash -e with a stub gh. Case lookup_fails (gh release view --json assets exits 1 with 'HTTP 502: Bad Gateway'): the output is that line, then 'No shared-name asset to remove.', exit 0, and no delete-asset call. Controls: delete_fails exits 1 (job fails); upload_fails exits 1 and the cleanup is not reached; shared_present deletes and exits 0; no_shared_asset and empty_release exit 0 without deleting. Fix: names=$(gh release view hail-store --json assets --jq '.assets[].name') || exit 1, then grep -qx on the variable.

findings.claim: A transient failure of a branch's own store asset (HTTP 503 after retries, or a network error) silently falls back to main's asset, so a --require-live branch build reads main's store and records the source as loaded.
findings.evidence: fetch_store_any moves to the next URL on any failure. Reproduction through website.build.hail_store with HAIL_STORE_ASSET=hail-store-claude-hail-b1.tar.gz, with the branch answer set to (None, 'not published (HTTP 404)'), (None, 'server error (HTTP 503)') or (None, 'ConnectionError'). Each time the fetcher was asked for hail-store-claude-hail-b1.tar.gz and then hail-store-main.tar.gz, the call returned index asset hail-store-main.tar.gz, and no exception was raised. Collector.hail (website/build.py line 262) then notes the source as ok unless the store is stale, so --require-live passes. Test coverage uses only the 404 answer (tests/test_site.py line 1923 and tests/test_hail.py line 1729). Fix: fall back only on 'not published (HTTP 404)' for a branch's own asset and raise on every other failure; keep main's single-asset path as it is.

findings.claim: The wait looks only at the store run of the same commit. A later commit that does not touch the store paths (for example a test fix) can build while an earlier commit's store run is still in progress, and then reads an older asset or fails spuriously.
findings.evidence: Reproduction: a stub gh answers 'in_progress null' for commit X and 'null null' for commit Y. The wait step run with GITHUB_SHA=Y exits 0 at once with 'No store job for this commit; the build reads the asset already published.' after one gh call. Preconditions in the YAML: the Website tests step (lines 93-95) precedes the wait (line 97), and a failed step stops the job, so a build that fails in its tests leaves its store run going; the concurrency group (line 41) is per branch, so the next commit's build starts when that one fails; the store paths (hail-store.yml lines 19-24) do not cover test files. Two outcomes: an older asset is read with no wait, or, when the branch's first asset and main's are both absent (before the merge), the fallback raises 'HailStoreError: the history download failed: hail-store-claude-hail-b1.tar.gz: not published (HTTP 404); hail-store-main.tar.gz: not published (HTTP 404)'. Store runs of one branch have overlapped in practice (B2 runs 39207568491 and 39209467411, under the old workflow). Fix: also wait for the branch's latest store run, for example gh run list --branch with GITHUB_REF_NAME.

findings.claim: On main the wait delays the public publish by the rest of the store run, and the build holds the main group meanwhile, so a scheduled publish that falls in the store window goes out late.
findings.evidence: The deploy job needs build (line 223), so Pages keeps the previous deploy until the build finishes. Store runs measured through the API: 10.7 minutes (run 39133848230, 2026-10-18) and 35.6 minutes (run 39355361340, 2026-10-20). The main group is held meanwhile (lines 40-41). Eleven scheduled main runs from 2026-10-20 05:23 to 2026-10-21 22:48 UTC have a mean gap of about 4.1 hours, so a 36-minute store window overlaps a scheduled start on roughly one store day in seven (an estimate from that cadence, not measured). The GitHub concurrency docs say a newly queued run replaces the pending one, so the scheduled runs queued in that window are replaced. D34 says only that main waits, not that the public publish is late. Fix: on main, read the last published asset without waiting (the store is rebuilt daily, so it is at most a day behind), or record the freshness cost in D34.

findings.claim: Branch names are not mapped to distinct asset names: claude/hail/b1 and claude/hail-b1 both publish and read hail-store-claude-hail-b1.tar.gz, and both match the claude/** push filter.
findings.evidence: The tr '/' '-' formula gives hail-store-claude-hail-b1.tar.gz for claude/hail-b1, claude/hail/b1 and claude-hail-b1 alike (bash output). The store concurrency group is per ref, so the two store jobs can run at once, and the later upload clobbers the other branch's asset. Fix: a reversible encoding of the slash, or reject ambiguous names.

findings.claim: The wait's progress messages print raw jq output ('queued null', 'in_progress null') instead of plain words.
findings.evidence: Reproduction output: 'The store job is queued null; waiting a minute.' and 'The store job is in_progress null; waiting a minute.' The owner's plain-words rule applies. Fix: map the states to words.

findings.claim: A store run superseded by a newer run in the same group is cancelled, and on a branch the wait then fails the build.
findings.evidence: Reproduction: 'completed cancelled' gives 'The store job ended as: completed cancelled. Read its log in the Actions tab.' with exit 1 on a branch and exit 0 on main. The GitHub concurrency docs say a newly queued run replaces the pending one. Fix: on a branch, read the newest store run for the branch, not only the run for the commit.

findings.claim: The 60-check bound has an off-by-one: after the 60th check the step sleeps and then reports 'still running' without checking again.
findings.evidence: The loop checks, then sleeps, for 60 iterations, then prints the failure text (lines 110-123). tests/test_site.py line 1903 asserts exactly 60 gh calls for the forever case, so there is no 61st check. A store run that ends during that last minute is reported as still running, and a branch build fails. Fix: sleep only between checks.

findings.claim: The gh calls in the wait have no timeout, so a stalled API call would hold the build to the 75-minute job timeout, which cancels it and skips the main deploy.
findings.evidence: Line 111 has no timeout wrapper. git show claude/hail-b5:.github/workflows/hail-store.yml lines 330-366 wrap gh calls in timeout --kill-after=30. gh's own default timeout was not measured. Fix: wrap the call in timeout.

result.notes:
Scope and verification (worktree /home/user/hail-b1/wt, branch claude/hail-b1; nothing edited, staged, committed or pushed; the worktree still shows the same 12 modified files and no untracked files). Scratch and logs: /home/user/hail-b1/out/review-live3/reviewer-ci/ (publish-run.sh, run-cases.sh, wait-run.sh, targeted-tests.log, ci-modules.log, bin/ stubs).

Verified, no finding:
- Both workflow files parse (PyYAML 6.0.1). Job timeouts: store 60 minutes (line 36), build 75 (line 47), deploy 10 (line 226).
- The requested command, exact: PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 /home/user/hail-b1/venv/bin/python -m unittest tests.test_site -k wait_step -k asset_the_same -k falls_back; tail: 'Ran 3 tests in 11.531s' then 'OK'.
- The Website offline test module set (test_site, test_gridded, test_basemap, test_storm, test_satellite, test_hail, test_website_workflow): 'Ran 553 tests in 121.221s', OK, no skips and no failures.
- The flags and JSON fields the workflows use exist in the local gh 2.89.0: run list --commit and --workflow, release view --json assets, release delete-asset --yes, release upload --clobber.
- Timeout arithmetic with measured steps (website run 39355361294, branch build): set-up to tests 2.1 minutes, build to keep 4.2 minutes. The wait is at most about 61 minutes, so the worst case is about 67 minutes against the 75-minute limit. It holds.
- The wait's bound covers a store run that starts together with the build. A store run that queues for more than about 3 minutes before it starts, then runs its full 60-minute cap, would outlast the bound. Queue times were not measured.
- The asset-name formula is identical in the store job and the build (the test checks it, and I reproduced it).
- Main's first build after the merge: origin/main has no hail-store.yml yet, so the 12:43 schedule starts only after the merge. The merge changes website/hail.py, so the store job runs on the merge commit and the build waits for it. If that store run fails, main still publishes (exit 0) and shows the unavailable text, as reproduced.
- A docs-only branch with no store job: the wait returns 'No store job', and the build reads the branch's asset if one exists, else main's. Before the merge the 404 failure is expected.
- Documented limit, consistent with the code (D34): a branch's own asset older than three days fails --require-live even when main's asset is fresh, because the fallback only follows a failed download. Expect this in long-lived previews.
- The release now holds only hail-store.tar.gz (the B3 data). hail-store-main.tar.gz and hail-store-claude-hail-b1.tar.gz do not exist yet.

Not verified: the length of the clobber window; gh's default network timeout; the outcome of main's first store run; the test counts quoted in the docs (594, 597). The CI step runs 553 tests; I did not count the full discover run. The release and run data come from the REST API, because gh release view uses GraphQL, which this session blocks.

No blocking finding: I found no path where the new code makes main's publish fail. The main wait exits 0 on every failure, and the exception paths I traced in the hail store code are caught.
